Title: Diagnosis of test `testContainsAny_StringWithBadSupplementaryChars`
Details:
The failing test `testContainsAny_StringWithBadSupplementaryChars` in `StringUtilsEqualsIndexOfTest` verifies if the method `StringUtils.containsAny` returns false when given input strings with broken supplementary characters -- specifically half of a supplementary character paired with a valid supplementary character.

Looking into the implementation of `StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, String)`, it delegates the operation to `containsAny(CharSequence, char[])`, which does the actual search. In `containsAny(CharSequence, char[])`, it iterates through each character of the input CharSequence and checks if it appears in the search character array.

If a high surrogate character (part of a supplementary character) is encountered, it attempts to check the next character as the low surrogate for a supplementary pair. If the search character after the current one in the array matches the following character in the CharSequence, it returns true; otherwise, if the current character is a basic multilingual plane character (non-surrogate), it returns true immediately upon match.

The problem likely arises due to how broken supplementary characters (only a high surrogate without a valid matching low surrogate) are handled. The code currently expects a matched pair of surrogate characters in sequence, comparing the next character of both sequences to confirm a supplementary character. If the input `CharUSuppCharLow` effectively breaks this assumption (being only a half surrogate or broken surrogate), this could cause the logic to improperly return true or false incorrectly instead of false as expected by the test.

Therefore, the bug is related to the handling of broken supplementary characters in the method `StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[])`. It does not adequately check or reject cases where surrogate pairs are incomplete or broken, and this incorrect handling leads to test failure.

---
Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsAny(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
